title: Post-COVID Life Sciences Transformation — Digital Investment and Engagement Shifts
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated digital transformation in life sciences by compressing years of change into months. 85.2% of companies reported higher planned digital investment post-pandemic. 69.5% of HCPs reported preference for fewer face-to-face interactions. Decentralized clinical trials gained momentum. The industry shifted from 'digital as supplement' to 'digital as default engagement model.'

findings.digital_investment_surge: 85.2% of life sciences companies reported higher planned digital investment compared to pre-pandemic levels. Investment concentrated in HCP engagement platforms, virtual events infrastructure, and data analytics.
findings.hcp_preference_shift: 69.5% of HCPs reported preference for fewer face-to-face rep interactions. Preference driven by time efficiency, on-demand content access, and reduced disruption to clinical workflows.
findings.decentralized_trials: Decentralized and hybrid clinical trial models accelerated. Remote monitoring, electronic patient-reported outcomes (ePRO/eCOA), and virtual site models moved from experimental to production.
findings.key_transformation_themes: Virtual engagement as the default channel; data-driven HCP targeting replacing geographic territory models; patient-centric trial design with remote participation options; digital-first commercial launch models for new products.
findings.permanent_behavior_change: Post-pandemic HCP digital preferences are persisting, not reverting. Organizations that treated digital as a temporary pandemic measure are falling behind those that restructured permanently.

title: Customer Advisory Board Insights — Clinical Persona Digital Engagement Requirements
summary: September 2022 customer advisory board with 11 pharma companies (Chiesi, Theramex, Pierre-Fabre, Zentiva, Ferring, Novo Nordisk, Roche, AstraZeneca, Vifor, Bayer, Merz) explored clinical persona requirements for digital-first engagement. COVID vaccine trial learnings informed commercial engagement strategy. Participants identified gaps in current CRM platforms for supporting medical affairs and clinical liaison workflows.

findings.participating_companies: Chiesi, Theramex, Pierre-Fabre, Zentiva, Ferring, Novo Nordisk, Roche, AstraZeneca, Vifor, Bayer, Merz — mix of large pharma and mid-market specialty companies.
findings.clinical_persona_gaps: Current CRM platforms designed primarily for commercial rep workflows. Clinical personas (MSLs, medical affairs, clinical liaisons) have different engagement patterns, compliance requirements, and content needs.
findings.vaccine_trial_learnings: COVID vaccine trial operations provided real-world validation of remote engagement, digital consent, and virtual monitoring capabilities at unprecedented scale.
findings.digital_first_requirements: Clinical personas require: integrated scientific content libraries, publication tracking, investigator meeting management, adverse event capture, and medical inquiry routing — functions that extend beyond standard CRM call reporting.
